justification: The run delivered a strong, technically consistent opening set on floors 2–4 and most of the ground floor, but left the ground-floor controlled north administrative wing without either of its intended access doors. Because that use group has six room doors into an otherwise disconnected spine, this is a Blocking access failure under the doors and windows standard and caps the result at 5.
evidence: Live measurements found 134 doors and 232 windows: floor 1 has 35/53, floors 2–4 have 33/59, 33/59, and 33/61. The ground-floor north administrative spine has doors only to six controlled rooms and no door to the civic orientation hall or outside; the agent also explicitly reported: “Still to place: 2 doors: the double door from the north administrative spine to the hall, and the staff entrance at the north end of the spine.”
strengths: All 366 delivered openings are hosted in walls; no unhosted opening was found on any occupied storey.
Upper-floor coverage is complete: each of floors 2–4 has 33 doors, no room without a door in the access check, and 59–61 exterior windows.
All windows read as exterior fixed windows, with consistent approximately 0.894 m sills and 2.706 m heads relative to each storey.
Door operations and nominal widths suit their roles: ordinary and stair doors are about 1.029 m, double doors about 1.943 m, and lift landing doors are sliding and about 1.200 m wide.
The opening check reported no shared-rule findings. Room doors open into their rooms, ground exits open outside, and lift doors are non-swinging.
The main entrance is a 1.943 m double-swing pair, and sampled stair and exit doors use the Single Flush Door family with a 60-minute fire rating.
The two rooms named as missing one planned window—Digital Assistance and Civic Exhibition—still each have an exterior fixed window, so they are not left without daylight.
The agent accurately disclosed the incomplete ground-floor openings rather than claiming a fully complete delivery.
weaknesses: Ground floor is incomplete by two doors and four windows; the two doors are the consequential omission.
The controlled north administrative spine has six office doors but no connection to the civic orientation hall or an exterior staff entrance, leaving that entire use group without a usable approach.

Ground-floor access verification is compromised by the run’s surrounding floor fragmentation: the access check reported the main entrance unresolved against an unconverted sketch room. This was used only as context, not scored as a general architectural defect.
Moving-leaf collision clearance was not assessable from the opening measurements; many leaf positions were explicitly reported as estimated, and the screenshots failed.

spec_violations.constraint: Every occupied use group must be enterable through a real door from circulation or outside.
spec_violations.what_happened: The ground-floor controlled north administrative spine and its six connected rooms have neither the planned hall connection nor the planned staff entrance.
spec_violations.evidence: The live opening graph lists six office doors on “F01-municipal-hall: Controlled north administrative spine” but no door to the civic orientation hall or outside.

spec_violations.constraint: Provide suitable door and window coverage throughout every occupied storey.
spec_violations.what_happened: Floor 1 remains short by two doors and four planned windows, although the affected habitable rooms still retain at least one exterior window.
spec_violations.evidence: Measured floor-1 count is 35 doors and 53 windows; the agent disclosed “ground 35 of 37” and “Still to place…4 windows.”
